newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices rise on tight supplies - trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices rise on tight supplies - trade.

text.p: Tight rubber supplies due to heavy monsoon rains in southern producing areas and Japanese buying pushed Thai rubber prices up this week, trade sources said on Friday.
The benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted around $1.24-1.25 a kg FOB Bangkok compared with around $1.23-1.24 a week earlier.
February deliveries also edged up to $1.24-$1.25 from $1.24 and latex rose to $0.94 per kg from $0.93 a week earlier.
But STR20 for January shipment barely changed from last week on thin demand as China, its traditional buyer, was absent.
"It seemed that Japan entered the market to buy the product before the holiday season," one Bangkok traders said.
However, the buying was limited by the quality of sheet rubber which was affected by the rain.
"Japanese buyers are very picky on quality...Heavy rains at the moment raised moisture content and contamination in the sheets," said one Hat Yai trader.
Many traders said they expected tight supplies to continue to support prices next week.
